Q: Tcl/Tk: 'moveto' position is off? A:

moveto uses ItemTranslate which most items specify for themselves.

Following the issue in the source-code leads to TranslateLine where we can find:

Side effects:

The position of the line is offset by (xDelta, yDelta), and the bounding box is updated in the generic part of the item structure.

The conclusion is that moveto doesn't update the coordinates, it updates the bbox so that the upper-left corner of the bounding box is at the given position. Which can be proven by using the bbox command:

     line
bbox =  (-2, -2, 12, 2)
coords =  [0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 0.0]
bbox =  (0, 0, 14, 4)
coords =  [2.0, 2.0, 12.0, 2.0]
     rectangle
bbox =  (-1, -1, 11, 2)
coords =  [0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 0.0]
bbox =  (0, 0, 12, 3)
coords =  [1.0, 1.0, 11.0, 1.0]
     text
bbox =  (-1, -7, 1, 8)
coords =  [0.0, 0.0]
bbox =  (0, 0, 2, 15)
coords =  [1.0, 7.0]

It is advisable to use move if you got multiple coordinate, such as coords=x1,y1,x2,y2.
moveto comes in handy if you are just provided with a location, such as coords=x1,y1.
Items with a location, such as text,window,image and bitmap, have an anchor option where you rather work with the bounding box instead of the coordinates.

Q: Way to decrypt with Jasypt spring.cloud.aws.credentials.access-key, spring.cloud.aws.credentials.secret-key before calling AWS parameter store? A:

Spring Cloud AWS reads spring.cloud.aws.credentials.* before Jasypt ever kicks in.
That means anything wrapped in ENC(...) for the access key or secret key will never be decrypted in time. Putting them in bootstrap.yml doesn't help either because Jasypt is initialized after the AWS client configuration phase.

In short: you can’t use Jasypt to decrypt the AWS credentials that are needed during bootstrap.

Recommended alternative is IAM roles, if your app runs on EC2, ECS, or EKS, assign an IAM role to the instance/task/pod.

Q: How can I make my button be clicked so my viewer can see a prompt box A:

Several things

  1. getElementsByClassName is plural see this question and should have been one of these document.getElementsByClassName('.btn')[0];
    document.querySelector('.btn');
    I prefer ID instead

  2. You need the code to be executed AFTER the button exists, either put the code tag after the HTML or wrap the code in
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { /* your code here */ });

  3. Your event listener is better coded like this

function recieveInputs() {
  let inputDigits = prompt("Number of squares you need");
  console.log(inputDigits,"squares");
}

const input = document.getElementById("btn");
input.addEventListener('click', recieveInputs);
<div class="butt">
  <button id="btn">Input Number</button>
</div>

Q: How to schedule multiple jobs from multiple properties files in Java Spring? A:

you can try to it this way in yml file :

@Scheduled(cron = "${spring.cron.jobs.history-cron.cron}") //usage

cron:
  jobs:
    stock-cron:
      cron: "0 0 */2 * * ?"
    history-cron:
      cron: "0 0/11 * * * *".
